$comment: ★ TF-C111 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION P3): `library.pe` is now ucrtbase.dll — this file moved with the whole co-state group (malloc/stdlib/string/stdio/io/errno/direct/process/sys-stat in ONE commit). It belongs to that group because `_fstat*` takes an `int fd`, an index into the OWNING runtime's descriptor table: an fd minted by io.json's `_open` on one CRT and handed to the other's `_fstat` resolves against a table that never saw it. That is not hypothetical — it is how this descriptor GOT into the group: a half-flip (sys/stat on ucrtbase, io still msvcrt) crashed the SQLite corpus at vtabH-3.5 with 0xC0000409, reproduced standalone. ★★ TWO RENAMES THE FLIP FORCED: plain `_wstat` and plain `_fstat` are msvcrt-ONLY (MEASURED, `objdump -p`; ucrtbase exports neither), so leaving them would have broken every pe binary's LOAD at 0xC0000139 (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT). They become `_wstat64i32` / `_fstat64i32`, with the legacy spellings kept alive as pe MACROS — which is EXACTLY what MSVC's own <sys/stat.h> does under the default undefined `_USE_32BIT_TIME_T` (`#define _fstat _fstat64i32`, `#define _wstat _wstat64i32`). ZERO struct churn: `64i32` means TIME64 timestamps + a 32-bit `st_size`, which is precisely the 48B `struct _stat` pe variant already declared below (== MSVC's `struct _stat64i32`), so the shapes already matched byte-for-byte and only the names moved. The `64i32` suffix is LOAD-BEARING — the plain-`64` spellings exist in BOTH DLLs and would link cleanly, then write a 64-bit `st_size` into the declared 32-bit field and shift every timestamp after it. ★ `_fstat64` is a SEPARATE, ADDITIONAL symbol (not the rename): the 56B time64+size64 form, needed by sqlite shell.c:25276 for the upcoming CLI capability, dual-exported (both DLLs) and paired with the `_stat64`/`__stat64` records already declared below. It lands here rather than after the CLI work precisely so it carries zero legacy debt. | c106 pe: struct _stat(the 48B _stat64i32 shape backing the x64 _wstat export — c106-audit runtime-probed msvcrt.dll: _wstat writes 48B, TIME64 not time32; {dev u32@0, ino u16@4, mode u16@6, nlink/uid/gid i16@8/10/12, [pad2], rdev u32@16, size i32@20, atime i64@24, mtime i64@32, ctime i64@40} — a 36B time32 _stat overran the caller's local by 12B AND mis-read mtime@28=atime-high=0/ctime@32=mtime-low) + _stat64/__stat64(56B time64+size64, BOTH tags; probe-confirmed) + _wstat/_stat64/_fstat64 + _S_IF* (ucrt); the 5 POSIX fns per-symbol gated [elf,macho] (loader law); st_atime/mtime/ctime flattening macros VARIANT-gated [elf,macho] (flat, they rewrote pe member access into st_*tim_sec). |Neutral shipped <sys/stat.h> (POSIX) — the FIRST real consumer of the plan-25 PER-TARGET struct `variants` mechanism. `struct stat` has a byte layout that DIVERGES per target: glibc x86-64-linux is 144 bytes (st_nlink is a 64-bit field at offset 16; st_mode at 24, after a 4-byte __pad0 that 8-aligns st_rdev), while glibc arm64-linux is 128 bytes (st_mode at 16, st_nlink a 32-bit field at 20; st_blksize is 32-bit with a __pad2). libc's fstat() writes the REAL struct and the program reads fields at OUR offsets, so a single layout would silently corrupt data on the other arch — the variant selector picks the field list matching (arch, format). The explicit padding fields (__pad0/__pad1/__pad2/reserved) make the layout engine's natural-alignment derivation reproduce the exact glibc offsets (sizeof = 144 / 128 respectively). The nested `struct timespec` (st_atim/mtim/ctim) is FLATTENED to its two i64 components (_sec/_nsec) here — bit-identical layout (timespec is {i64,i64}, 16 bytes); the real nested-timespec field names are a c14 authoring detail. Field types are RESOLVED hir-text builtins. c15c adds the macОS variant `when:{format:macho}` — the Darwin 64-bit-inode `struct stat` (verified against xnu/bsd/sys/stat.h): 144 bytes, the SAME SIZE as x86-64-linux but a COMPLETELY different layout (st_dev i32@0, st_mode/st_nlink uint16@4/6, st_ino u64@8, st_rdev i32@24 + a 4-byte __pad0@28 to 8-align FOUR timespecs incl. st_birthtimespec@80, st_blksize i32@112, the st_qspare tail) — the dangerous same-size swap the c13 lesson flagged (a size-only check would not catch it; the corpus pins a FIELD offset). arm64-macho and x86_64-macho are byte-identical (all fixed-width) so one `when:{format:macho}` covers both. The S_* constants + S_IS* macros + st_*time macros AGREE Linux↔macOS (the st_*tim_sec flat field names are shared). ★★ TF-C121 (D-FFI-SHIPPED-SYMBOL-PER-TARGET-LINK-NAME) — fstat/lstat/stat now carry a per-target `linkName`, and the sentence that used to stand here was WRONG in the dangerous direction. It said the plain names were 'correct for arm64-macho … the x86_64-macho `$INODE64` asm-label alias is byte-pinned-only, no CI leg', i.e. it framed x86_64 as an unexercised residual. MEASURED, matched two-arch control on real Darwin (macOS 26.5.2, ONE TU, only `-arch` differs, `cc -c` then `nm -u`): x86_64 emits `_stat$INODE64 _fstat$INODE64 _lstat$INODE64`, arm64 emits `_stat _fstat _lstat` — because sys/cdefs.h makes `__DARWIN_ONLY_64_BIT_INO_T` 0 on x86_64 (so `__DARWIN_SUF_64_BIT_INO_T` = "$INODE64") and 1 on arm64 (suffix empty). Declaring the plain name on x86_64 does NOT fail loud: it binds the LEGACY 32-bit-inode implementation, which writes only 120 of the 144 bytes this file's macho `struct stat` variant declares. st_size is read at 96 and the legacy callee writes it at 72 ⇒ `fstat` returns st_size 0 ⇒ sqlite sees every database as empty ⇒ "database disk image is malformed". Proven whole-binary: the BYTE-IDENTICAL DSS x86_64 sqlite3 CLI went 3/7 → 7/7 under a DYLD_INTERPOSE shim that swapped ONLY the bindings, no recompile. The `_` is NOT written here — `linkName` declares the UNDECORATED base and `ffi::linkNameFor`/`applyCMangling` composes the format's underscore, the same single rule the un-overridden path takes. arm64 matches no variant and keeps the plain name (its only ABI is the modern one) — the matched control that must stay green. ★ AUTHORING RULE THIS CLASS FORCES: 'verify the symbol is exported' would NOT have caught it — BOTH `_fstat` and `_fstat$INODE64` exist in libSystem's x86_64 slice. The check is 'does a real compiler for THIS target emit THIS name for THIS C identifier'. This local row is a PER-DESCRIPTOR declaration, not a shared identity; closing that gap is D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-CROSS-FILE-TYPE-IDENTITY. It is a LOCAL row rather than a cross-descriptor import because the reader's name vocabulary is per-descriptor, and it is honest: POSIX requires <sys/stat.h> itself to define the timespec structure. Declared FLAT (no `variants`) so it is published on EVERY format — a format-gated dependency would make the whole `stat` entry unavailable on pe and take MSVC's `struct stat` down with it. ★ THE OVERLAY, AND WHY: st_mtimespec occupies THE SAME 16 bytes as the existing flat st_mtim_sec/st_mtim_nsec, which must STAY — the st_mtime macro above maps onto st_mtim_sec. Natural-alignment derivation can only APPEND, so the macho variant moves onto the c107 EXPLICIT-OFFSET channel (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-UNION-OVERLAY, all-or-none per variant): every field now states the byte offset it ALREADY had, and the three mtime members overlap at 48 exactly as Darwin's own `#define st_mtime st_mtimespec.tv_sec` overlays them.
